description:
## Symptom

While compaction is in flight, no visible animation indicates work is happening — the loader appears static.

## Cause (suspected)

`apps/octo_pi_tui/lib/octo_pi/tui/components/loader.ex:41` derives the Braille spinner frame from `System.monotonic_time(:millisecond) / 80ms`, so the *value* advances with wall-clock time — but only when the component is **re-rendered**.

`interactive.ex:1118` has a no-op `:loader_tick` handler, suggesting an animation tick is intended but may not be wired (or not fire when only `state.loader` is set with no streaming events).

## Upstream behavior

`tmp/pi-mono/packages/tui/src/components/loader.ts:17-85`: a dedicated `setInterval` at 80ms (`start()` lines 41-44) drives a re-render each tick. The animation does not depend on event traffic.

## Proposed fix

1. Confirm whether anything emits `:loader_tick` on an ~80ms cadence while a loader is mounted.
2. If not, add a periodic ticker that emits a re-render event while `state.loader != nil`. Mirror upstream's `intervalId` lifecycle: start on loader mount, stop on dismount.

## TDD plan

1. **Red — investigation test.** Write a test that mounts a loader and asserts that within ~250ms the interactive process has received at least 2 `:loader_tick` (or equivalent re-render) messages. Use telemetry / `assert_receive` — **no `Process.sleep`** for the assertion (per project rule); use `assert_receive` with timeout.
2. **Red — frame-advance test.** With the above ticker in place, render the loader at t=0 and again after a tick is processed; assert the spinner frame character differs. (The frame derivation is monotonic-time based, so this is a state-machine + rerender contract test, not a pure unit test.)
3. **Green.** Add the loader-tick scheduler and dismount logic.
4. **Validate.** Run a long `/compact` in tmux; spinner animates smoothly.
title: No animated spinner while compaction runs
